\\"60px\\"\\n---\\n\\n# Design System: LSAT Academy\\n\\n## Overview\\n\\n**Creative North Star: \\"LSAT Academy\\"**\\n\\nOne institution with two registers, and the seam between them is deliberate.\\n\\n**The Hall** is the door. Unauthenticated, dark, and material: near-black ground, warm marble text, a bronze that carries the light, and a serif that behaves like carved lettering. Its own source calls it a museum nocturne, carved marble filmed in darkness, read by modern instruments. Its job is to make a prospective student feel they are entering somewhere, not signing up for something. It is the only place in the product where atmosphere outranks throughput.\\n\\n**The Workroom** is everything past sign-in. Light, neutral, and quiet, because a student sits inside it for an hour reading dense argument text and the interface must not compete with the passage. There is no warmth here and that is the decision, not an oversight: warm accents need a dark ground to read, and on the Workroom\'s white they collapse. The Hall\'s bronze measures 8.58:1 on its own night and 2.30:1 on the Workroom\'s page. The two registers do not share a palette because they cannot.\\n\\nWhat they do share is restraint about meaning. In both, colour is a signal. Green, red and amber say something happened. Nothing is coloured to be warm, to look premium, or to fill a space. Depth comes from hairlines and background tone rather than shadow, and hierarchy comes from size, weight and position rather than hue.\\n\\nInside the Workroom, individual rooms may commit fully to their own world. The eight Activity Centre worlds, the scoped bootcamps and…276 tokens truncated…`): the Hall\'s cool instrument note against the bronze, and the colour of its focus outlines. Rare by design; it marks precision where bronze marks warmth.\\n- **Teacher Amber** (`#c7841f`): the single accent of the teacher workspace, with a hue-locked ramp for hover (`#af7318`), text on tinted fills (`#895910`) and a light step (`#e0a648`). Deliberately theme-independent: the workspace is always the light format. It is the one accent in the product, and it belongs to the operator, not the student.\\n\\n### Tertiary\\n\\nIndividual rooms carry their own palettes behind a wrapper class and are documented in their own surface briefs, not here. The wrappers in use are `.classroom-root`, `.mc-bootcamp`, `.ff-bootcamp`, `.rc-bootcamp`, `.topic-abstract`, `.cs-punk`, and the eight Activity Centre worlds.\\n\\n`.classroom-root` was added to this list on 2026-09-08, after an audit found the classroom running on Outfit and a warm palette while this record still described it as neutral Workroom chrome. It is a sanctioned world, not drift: the warmth and the typeface are deliberate and they are what makes the classroom feel like a study rather than a dashboard. The record was wrong, not the code. Its brief is `.impeccable/surfaces/classroom.md`. Note that this is the one sanctioned world that is also a corridor, so the rule below about corridors never being worlds now has exactly one documented exception.\\n\\n### Neutral\\n\\n- **Workroom Page** (`#fcfcfc`) and **Card** (`#ffffff`): the page ground and the surface that sits on it. One step of separation, no more.\\n- **Workroom Raised** (`#f7f7f7`) and **Fill** (`#f2f2f2`): the two tonal steps available for layering and for resting fills.\\n- **Workroom Ink Muted** (`#737373`): secondary text. Measures 4.62:1 on the page, which clears the floor with almost nothing to spare. Do not lighten it.\\n- **Workroom Hairline** (`#e0e0e0`) and **Field** (`#e6e6e6`): the borders that do the work shadows used to.\\n- **Hall Marble** (`#eae5da`), with secondary (`#a6a093`) and muted (`#6e695e`) steps: warm off-white text on the night ground.\\n\\n### State (semantic only, never decorative)\\n\\n- **Correct** (`#10b77f`) and **Incorrect** (`#f43e5c`): a student\'s attempt was right or wrong. Held under their own names, separate from system status, so a future shift to one cannot silently reframe the other.\\n- **Warn** (`#f59f0a`): a bonus, a stretch, a non-blocking notice.\\n- **Success** (`#21c45d`), **Warning** (`#f59f0a`), **Destructive** (`#dc2828`): system status, not student performance.\\n\\n### Named Rules\\n\\n**The Ground Decides Rule.** A warm colour is legible on the Hall\'s night and illegible on the Workroom\'s page. Never carry a colour across the seam on the strength of liking it; measure it against the ground it will land on first.\\n\\n**The Meaning-Only Rule.** A colour appears in the Workroom because something is right, wrong, cautionary, or dangerous. There is no fifth reason. If a surface feels flat and the impulse is to add a colour, the answer is type and space.\\n\\n**The Named Ground Rule.** No colour is written as a literal hex in a component. It resolves from a token, and a token that resolves to nothing is a defect, not a subtle effect. Three colour names in this codebase pointed at variables that were never defined, and the product silently lost its focus ring for five months.\\n\\n## Typography\\n\\n**Workroom Body:** Lexend (with Outfit, then the system stack)\\n**Hall Display:** Fraunces (with Iowan Old Style, Times New Roman, serif)\\n**Hall Inscription:** Cinzel (with Trajan Pro, serif)\\n**Mono:** IBM Plex Mono\\n**Question Lock:** Outfit, held deliberately for LSAT question surfaces\\n\\n**Character:** The Workroom is one humanist sans doing everything, sized and weighted rather than swapped. The Hall is a serif institution: an optical serif for its headings and an inscriptional face for its few carved lines. The split is the whole typographic idea. Inside, type gets out of the way; at the door, type is the architecture.\\n\\n### Hierarchy\\n\\n- **Title** (600, 24px, line-height 1, tracking -0.025em): card and section headings in the Workroom.\\n- **Body** (400, 14px rising to 16px at 640px and above, line-height 1.6): everything a student reads in the Workroom chrome.\\n- **Question** (400, 16px, line-height 1.6, Outfit): LSAT stimulus and answer choices. Font-locked to Outfit even though the rest of the app moved to Lexend, so question text does not shift when the shell\'s face changes.\\n- **Label** (500, 14px): button and control labels.\\n- **Hall Display** (380, fluid, tracking -0.015em, Fraunces): Hall headings. The unusually light 380 weight is the point; it reads as carved rather than printed.\\n- **Hall Inscription** (500, tracking 0.05em, Cinzel): the Hall\'s few short carved lines. Never body copy.\\n- **Hall Mono** (400, 13px, tracking 0.04em, IBM Plex Mono): the Hall\'s instrument labels.\\n\\n### Named Rules\\n\\n**The One Face Rule.** The Workroom uses a single family. Hierarchy is built from size, weight and space. A second family inside the Workroom is a defect unless it is the Outfit question lock.\\n\\n**The Question Never Moves Rule.** LSAT question text is font-locked. A change to the shell\'s typeface must not reflow a passage a student is mid-way through reading.\\n\\n**The Serif Stays At The Door Rule.** Fraunces and Cinzel belong to the Hall. A serif appearing in the Workroom chrome means the seam has leaked.\\n\\n## Layout\\n\\nThe Workroom is a centred single column with generous side gutters. The container centres by default, carries 32px of horizontal padding, and stops widening at 1400px.\\n\\nBreakpoints are the framework defaults up to 1280px, with the largest step pulled in to 1400px. Body type steps from 14px to 16px at 640px, and form controls are forced to 16px below 768px so that iOS does not zoom the page when a field takes focus. Named breakpoints `phone` (up to 600px), `tablet` (601 to 900px) and `desktop` (901px and up) exist for bootcamp surfaces.\\n\\nSpacing runs on a 4px base. The steps in real use are 4, 8, 16, 24 and 32. Card padding is 24px on all sides; button padding is 8px vertical and 16px horizontal.\\n\\nReading measure matters more here than in most products. Passage and stimulus text is held to a comfortable line length rather than allowed to run the full container width.\\n\\n### Named Rules\\n\\n**The Reading Measure Rule.** Any surface carrying an LSAT passage, stimulus, or explanation constrains its own line length. The container\'s maximum is a ceiling for layout, never a licence for prose.\\n\\n## Elevation & Depth\\n\\n**Flat, with hairline separation.** Surfaces sit on the page rather than above it. A card is distinguished from its ground by a one-pixel border and, where more is needed, by one step of background tone. There are no drop shadows in the Workroom.\\n\\nThis is a decision, not a description. The codebase currently ships five shadow tokens tuned for a dark ground, from `0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)` up to `0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.7)`, and applies the smallest of them to every card. Because the app ships light by default, those shadows land at 40 percent black under a white card. The light theme never redefined them, and the one glow token is white, so it is invisible on white. The tokens are retired by this record and the code has not caught up yet.\\n\\nThe Hall is the exception and keeps its own depth: fixed ambience gradients, a grain overlay, and an inset highlight on its call to action. That depth is atmospheric rather than structural, and it does not transfer.\\n\\n### Named Rules\\n\\n**The Flat Rule.** Depth in the Workroom comes from a hairline or a tonal step. A `box-shadow` on a Workroom surface is a defect.\\n\\n**The Two-Step Rule.** Page, then card, then at most one raised step. A surface that needs a fourth level of layering is a surface that needs restructuring.\\n\\n## Shapes\\n\\nCorners are gently rounded and consistent: 8px for cards and containers, 6px for buttons and inputs, 4px for the smallest chips and insets, and a full pill only for genuine badges. The scale derives from one 0.5rem radius token, so a change to the base moves the whole system together.\\n\\nThe Hall uses a near-square 2px radius instead. Its edges are cut, not softened, which is what separates a carved surface from a card.\\n\\nBorders are one pixel. There is no second border weight in the Workroom.\\n\\n### Named Rules\\n\\n**The Hairline Rule.** One pixel, always. A thicker border used as a coloured accent stripe on the leading edge of a surface is banned, including when faked with an inset shadow. Active state is carried by background tone.\\n\\n## Components\\n\\n### Buttons\\n\\n- **Character:** precise and quiet. A button is a plain rectangle with a label. It darkens slightly on hover and does nothing else. It does not lift, does not cast a shadow, and does not scale on press.\\n- **Shape:** gently rounded (6px).\\n- **Primary:** ink fill (`#121212`), page-coloured label, 8px by 16px padding.\\n- **Outline:** page background, one-pixel field border, ink label.\\n- **Ghost:** no fill at rest, a tonal fill on hover.\\n- **Sizes:** default 44px tall, small 40px, large 48px, icon 44 by 44. Every size clears the 44px touch minimum by being that height, never by relying on wrapped text or padding accidents.\\n- **Focus:** a solid two-pixel ink outline, offset two pixels from the edge. This is the only focus treatment in the Workroom.\\n- **Hall CTA:** 60px tall, near-square corners, transparent fill over a bronze hairline, with a bronze sheen that sweeps across on hover and a cyan outline on focus.\\n\\n### Cards / Containers\\n\\n- **Corner:** 8px.\\n- **Background:** card white on the page ground.\\n- **Border:** one-pixel hairline. This is what separates the card, not a shadow.\\n- **Shadow:** none.\\n- **Padding:** 24px, with header, content and footer sharing that inset.\\n\\n### Inputs / Fields\\n\\n- **Style:** page background, one-pixel field border, 6px corners, 44px minimum height, 8px by 12px padding.\\n- **Focus:** the same two-pixel ink outline as buttons, offset two pixels. Do not express focus as a border colour change alone; a border shift is too quiet to serve as the only indicator.\\n- **Mobile:** 16px text below 768px, so focusing a field never zooms the viewport.\\n\\n### Navigation\\n\\nNeutral chrome throughout. The sidebar runs one tonal step off the page ground with a hairline edge, and the active item is marked by background tone rather than by a coloured rule on its leading edge.\\n\\n### Signature Component: the scoped world\\n\\nThe product\'s distinctive pattern is not a control, it is a container. A room commits fully to its own palette, typefaces and atmosphere behind a single wrapper class, and nothing inside it leaks out. Scene layers are `aria-hidden` furniture painted beneath the content, so the accessible tree is identical whether the room is painted or bare. A new world is added by writing a new wrapper and its prefixed tokens, never by adding hex to a shared component.\\n\\n## Do\'s and Don\'ts\\n\\n### Do:\\n\\n- **Do** resolve every colour from a token, and treat a token that resolves to nothing as a defect. Verify a new token renders before documenting it.\\n- **Do** give every interactive element a visible focus indicator: a solid two-pixel ink outline offset two pixels in the Workroom, cyan in the Hall.\\n- **Do** check contrast against the ground the colour will actually land on, in the theme that actually ships, in a browser. The theme file has read as correct while the page rendered a light card on a near-black ground.\\n- **Do** separate surfaces with a one-pixel hairline and one tonal step.\\n- **Do** keep colour semantic: correct, incorrect, warning, danger. Nothing else earns it.\\n- **Do** scope a new room\'s identity behind its own wrapper class with prefixed tokens, the way the bootcamps and the eight Activity worlds already do.\\n- **Do** hold LSAT passage and stimulus text to a readable line length, and leave it on the Outfit question lock.\\n- **Do** end every world\'s stylesheet with a `prefers-reduced-motion` block that stops continuous motion rather than speeding it up.\\n\\n### Don\'t:\\n\\n- **Don\'t** add a `box-shadow` to a Workroom surface. Depth is hairline and tone.\\n- **Don\'t** carry a Hall colour into the Workroom. Bronze reads 8.58:1 on the Hall\'s night and 2.30:1 on the Workroom\'s page.\\n- **Don\'t** introduce a warm or metallic accent into the Workroom to make it feel premium. Premium here is depth, hierarchy and type.\\n- **Don\'t** remove the browser\'s focus outline without shipping a replacement in the same rule. `outline-none` with no working ring is worse than leaving the default alone.\\n- **Don\'t** animate the focus indicator. A `transition-all` on a control means the ring fades in, which delays the one signal a keyboard user depends on.\\n- **Don\'t** use a border thicker than one pixel as a coloured accent stripe, including when faked with an inset shadow.\\n- **Don\'t** put a second typeface into the Workroom chrome, and don\'t let a serif cross in from the Hall.\\n- **Don\'t** animate layout properties. Animate `opacity`, `transform` and `color`. No bounce, no elastic, no lift on hover.\\n- **Don\'t** write a hex value into a component. If a room needs its own colour, promote it to named tokens behind that room\'s wrapper.\\n\\n<!--\\nKnown gaps between this record and the code, as of 2026-09-05. Recorded rather\\nthan hidden; none of them were fixed by writing this file.\\n\\n1. FIXED 2026-09-05. The shared Button and Input had no visible focus indicator:\\n   `focus-visible:outline-none` worked, `focus-visible:ring-3` generated no CSS\\n   (Tailwind 3 has no `ring-3`), and `focus-visible:ring-accent-bronze/50` pointed at\\n   an undefined variable. Both now use `outline-2 outline-offset-2 outline-foreground`,\\n   and `transition-all` was narrowed so the ring no longer fades in. A zero-specificity\\n   `:where(...):focus-visible` floor in `src/index.css` catches any control that\\n   defines nothing, while still losing to the Hall\'s cyan and the scoped bootcamp rings.\\n   Verified in a browser on all five Button variants and the Input: 18.26:1 in light,\\n   18.97:1 in the dark alternate, against the 3:1 an indicator needs.\\n\\n2. FIXED 2026-09-05. `--accent-bronze`, `--accent-warm` and `--glow-bronze` were\\n   consumed by tailwind.config.ts and defined in no commit in the repo\'s history.\\n   They arrived 2026-04-06 in \\"Imported LSATATTORNEYS project files\\". `#b06a3e` was\\n   inferred from a literal rgba in the `glow-sm` shadow on 2026-06-26 and written into\\n   the previous DESIGN.md as a brand accent it never was. All three names and the\\n   bronze-literal `glow-sm` shadow are removed, and their thirteen call sites now use\\n   neutral tokens. Three of those call sites were visibly broken, not merely untokenized:\\n   the journal ReviewForm\'s Next button rendered near-white text on a transparent\\n   background, its active step dot was invisible while the inactive dots showed, and the\\n   Annotate toggle\'s active state was indistinguishable from its inactive state.\\n   `docs/chart-palette.md` and `scripts/validate-chart-palette.mjs` still carry the\\n   inherited hex and have not been touched.\\n\\n3. Shadow tokens are dark-tuned and the app ships light. `shadow-sm` puts\\n   rgba(0,0,0,0.4) under a white card. Retired above; still applied by `ui/card.tsx`.\\n\\n4. Contrast failures in the shipped light theme, measured: `--text-tertiary` 3.28:1,\\n   `--success` 2.24:1, `--warning` 2.08:1, `--state-correct` 2.53:1,\\n   `--state-incorrect` 3.60:1, `--teacher-accent` 3.03:1 as text. In the dark\\n   alternate, `--text-tertiary` 4.18:1. AA needs 4.5:1 for normal text.\\n\\n5. Components are tactile today, not quiet. Buttons lift, scale on press, and gain\\n   a shadow on hover; cards carry `shadow-sm`. Use 4pt for granularity: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96px.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Name Tokens Semantically\\r\\n\\r\\nName by relationship (`--space-sm`, `--space-lg`), not value (`--spacing-8`). Use `gap` instead of margins for sibling spacing—it eliminates margin collapse and cleanup hacks.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Grid Systems\\r\\n\\r\\n### The Self-Adjusting Grid\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))` for responsive grids without breakpoints. Columns are at least 280px, as many as fit per row, leftovers stretch. For complex layouts, use named grid areas (`grid-template-areas`) and redefine them at breakpoints.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Visual Hierarchy\\r\\n\\r\\n### The Squint Test\\r\\n\\r\\nBlur your eyes (or screenshot and blur). Can you still identify:\\r\\n- The most important element?\\r\\n- The second most important?\\r\\n- Clear groupings?\\r\\n\\r\\nIf everything looks the same weight blurred, you have a hierarchy problem.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Hierarchy Through Multiple Dimensions\\r\\n\\r\\nDon\'t rely on size alone. Combine:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Tool | Strong Hierarchy | Weak Hierarchy |\\r\\n|------|------------------|----------------|\\r\\n| **Size** | 3:1 ratio or more | <2:1 ratio |\\r\\n| **Weight** | Bold vs Regular | Medium vs Regular |\\r\\n| **Color** | High contrast | Similar tones |\\r\\n| **Position** | Top/left (primary) | Bottom/right |\\r\\n| **Space** | Surrounded by white space | Crowded |\\r\\n\\r\\n**The best hierarchy uses 2-3 dimensions at once**: A heading that\'s larger, bolder, AND has more space above it.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Cards Are Not Required\\r\\n\\r\\nCards are overused. Spacing and alignment create visual grouping naturally. Use cards only when content is truly distinct and actionable, items need visual comparison in a grid, or content needs clear interaction boundaries. **Never nest cards inside cards**—use spacing, typography, and subtle dividers for hierarchy within a card.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Container Queries\\r\\n\\r\\nViewport queries are for page layouts. **Container queries are for components**:\\r\\n\\r\\n```css\\r\\n.card-container {\\r\\n  container-type: inline-size;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n.card {\\r\\n  display: grid;\\r\\n  gap: var(--space-md);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Card layout changes based on its container, not viewport */\\r\\n@container (min-width: 400px) {\\r\\n  .card {\\r\\n    grid-template-columns: 120px 1fr;\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Why this matters**: A card in a narrow sidebar stays compact, while the same card in a main content area expands—automatically, without viewport hacks.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Optical Adjustments\\r\\n\\r\\nText at `margin-left: 0` looks indented due to letterform whitespace—use negative margin (`-0.05em`) to optically align. Geometrically centered icons often look off-center; play icons need to shift right, arrows shift toward their direction.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Touch Targets vs Visual Size\\r\\n\\r\\nButtons can look small but need large touch targets (44px minimum). Use padding or pseudo-elements:\\r\\n\\r\\n```css\\r\\n.icon-button {\\r\\n  width: 24px;  /* Visual size */\\r\\n  height: 24px;\\r\\n  position: relative;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n.icon-button::before {\\r\\n  content: \'\';\\r\\n  position: absolute;\\r\\n  inset: -10px;  /* Expand tap target to 44px */\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Depth & Elevation\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate semantic z-index scales (dropdown → sticky → modal-backdrop → modal → toast → tooltip) instead of arbitrary numbers. For shadows, create a consistent elevation scale (sm → md → lg → xl). **Key insight**: Shadows should be subtle—if you can clearly see it, it\'s probably too strong.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n**Avoid**: Arbitrary spacing values outside your scale. Making all spacing equal (variety creates hierarchy). Creating hierarchy through size alone - combine size, weight, color, and space.\\r\\n"}}}'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"i":2,"result":{"status":"fulfilled","value":{"chunk_id":"f8a76a","wall_time_seconds":1.3619226,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":2109,"output":"# Typography\\r\\n\\r\\n## Classic Typography Principles\\r\\n\\r\\n### Vertical Rhythm\\r\\n\\r\\nYour line-height should be the base unit for ALL vertical spacing. If body text has `line-height: 1.5` on `16px` type (= 24px), spacing values should be multiples of 24px. This creates subconscious harmony—text and space share a mathematical foundation.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Modular Scale & Hierarchy\\r\\n\\r\\nThe common mistake: too many font sizes that are too close together (14px, 15px, 16px, 18px...). This creates muddy hierarchy.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Use fewer sizes with more contrast.** A 5-size system covers most needs:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Role | Typical Ratio | Use Case |\\r\\n|------|---------------|----------|\\r\\n| xs | 0.75rem | Captions, legal |\\r\\n| sm | 0.875rem | Secondary UI, metadata |\\r\\n| base | 1rem | Body text |\\r\\n| lg | 1.25-1.5rem | Subheadings, lead text |\\r\\n| xl+ | 2-4rem | Headlines, hero text |\\r\\n\\r\\nPopular ratios: 1.25 (major third), 1.333 (perfect fourth), 1.5 (perfect fifth). Pick one and commit.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Readability & Measure\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `ch` units for character-based measure (`max-width: 65ch`). Line-height scales inversely with line length—narrow columns need tighter leading, wide columns need more.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Non-obvious**: Light text on dark backgrounds needs compensation on three axes, not just one. Bump line-height by 0.05–0.1, add a touch of letter-spacing (0.01–0.02em), and optionally step the body weight up one notch (regular → medium). The perceived weight drops across all three; fix all three.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Paragraph rhythm**: Pick either space between paragraphs OR first-line indentation. Never both. Digital usually wants space; editorial/long-form can justify indent-only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Font Selection & Pairing\\r\\n\\r\\nThe tactical selection procedure and the reflex-reject list live in [reference/brand.md](brand.md) under **Font selection procedure** and **Reflex-reject list** (loaded for brand-register tasks). The rest of this section covers the adjacent knowledge: anti-reflex corrections, system font use, and pairing rules.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Anti-reflexes worth defending against\\r\\n\\r\\n- A technical/utilitarian brief does NOT need a serif \\"for warmth.\\" Most tech tools should look like tech tools.\\r\\n- An editorial/premium brief does NOT need the same expressive serif everyone is using right now. Premium can be Swiss-modern, can be neo-grotesque, can be a literal monospace, can be a quiet humanist sans.\\r\\n- A children\'s product does NOT need a rounded display font. Kids\' books use real type.\\r\\n- A \\"modern\\" brief does NOT need a geometric sans. The most modern thing you can do is not use the font everyone else is using.\\r\\n\\r\\n**System fonts are underrated**: `-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, \\"Segoe UI\\", system-ui` looks native, loads instantly, and is highly readable. Consider this for apps where performance > personality.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Pairing Principles\\r\\n\\r\\n**The non-obvious truth**: You often don\'t need a second font. One well-chosen font family in multiple weights creates cleaner hierarchy than two competing typefaces. Only add a second font when you need genuine contrast (e.g., display headlines + body serif).\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen pairing, contrast on multiple axes:\\r\\n- Serif + Sans (structure contrast)\\r\\n- Geometric + Humanist (personality contrast)\\r\\n- Condensed display + Wide body (proportion contrast)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Never pair fonts that are similar but not identical** (e.g., two geometric sans-serifs). They create visual tension without clear hierarchy.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Web Font Loading\\r\\n\\r\\nThe layout shift problem: fonts load late, text reflows, and users see content jump. Here\'s the fix:\\r\\n\\r\\n```css\\r\\n/* 1. Use font-display: swap for visibility */\\r\\n@font-face {\\r\\n  font-family: \'CustomFont\';\\r\\n  src: url(\'font.woff2\') format(\'woff2\');\\r\\n  font-display: swap;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* 2. Match fallback metrics to minimize shift */\\r\\n@font-face {\\r\\n  font-family: \'CustomFont-Fallback\';\\r\\n  src: local(\'Arial\');\\r\\n  size-adjust: 105%;        /* Scale to match x-height */\\r\\n  ascent-override: 90%;     /* Match ascender height */\\r\\n  descent-override: 20%;    /* Match descender depth */\\r\\n  line-gap-override: 10%;   /* Match line spacing */\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nbody {\\r\\n  font-family: \'CustomFont\', \'CustomFont-Fallback\', sans-serif;\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nTools like [Fontaine](https://github.com/unjs/fontaine) calculate these overrides automatically.\\r\\n\\r\\n**`swap` vs `optional`**: `swap` shows fallback text immediately and FOUT-swaps when the web font arrives. `optional` uses the fallback if the web font misses a small load budget (~100ms) and avoids the shift entirely. Pick `optional` when zero layout shift matters more than seeing the branded font on slow networks.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Preload the critical weight only**: typically the regular-weight body font used above the fold. Preloading every weight costs more bandwidth than it saves.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Variable fonts for 3+ weights or styles**: a single variable font file is usually smaller than three static weight files, gives fractional weight control, and pairs well with `font-optical-sizing: auto`. For 1–2 weights, static is fine.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Modern Web Typography\\r\\n\\r\\n### Fluid Type\\r\\n\\r\\nFluid typography via `clamp(min, preferred, max)` scales text smoothly with the viewport. The middle value (e.g., `5vw + 1rem`) controls scaling rate—higher vw = faster scaling. Add a rem offset so it doesn\'t collapse to 0 on small screens.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Use fluid type for**: Headings and display text on marketing/content pages where text dominates the layout and needs to breathe across viewport sizes.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Use fixed `rem` scales for**: App UIs, dashboards, and data-dense interfaces. No major app design system (Material, Polaris, Primer, Carbon) uses fluid type in product UI — fixed scales with optional breakpoint adjustments give the spatial predictability that container-based layouts need. Body text should also be fixed even on marketing pages, since the size difference across viewports is too small to warrant it.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Bound your clamp()**: keep `max-size ≤ ~2.5 × min-size`. Wider ratios break the browser\'s zoom and reflow behaviour and make large viewports feel like the page is shouting.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Scale container width and font-size together** so effective character measure stays in the 45–75ch band at every viewport. A heading that widens faster than its container drifts out of the comfortable measure at the top end.\\r\\n\\r\\n### OpenType Features\\r\\n\\r\\nMost developers don\'t know these exist. Use them for polish:\\r\\n\\r\\n```css\\r\\n/* Tabular numbers for data alignment */\\r\\n.data-table { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Proper fractions */\\r\\n.recipe-amount { font-variant-numeric: diagonal-fractions; }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Small caps for abbreviations */\\r\\nabbr { font-variant-caps: all-small-caps; }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Disable ligatures in code */\\r\\ncode { font-variant-ligatures: none; }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Enable kerning (usually on by default, but be explicit) */\\r\\nbody { font-kerning: normal; }\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nCheck what features your font supports at [Wakamai Fondue](https://wakamaifondue.com/).\\r\\n\\r\\n### Rendering polish\\r\\n\\r\\n```css\\r\\n/* Even out heading line lengths (browser picks better break points) */\\r\\nh1, h2, h3 { text-wrap: balance; }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Reduce orphans and ragged endings in long prose */\\r\\narticle p { text-wrap: pretty; }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Variable fonts: pick the right optical-size master automatically */\\r\\nbody { font-optical-sizing: auto; }\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**ALL-CAPS tracking**: capitals sit too close at default spacing. Add 5–12% letter-spacing (`letter-spacing: 0.05em` to `0.12em`) to short all-caps labels, eyebrows, and small headings. Real small caps (via `font-variant-caps`) need the same treatment, slightly gentler.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Typography System Architecture\\r\\n\\r\\nName tokens semantically (`--text-body`, `--text-heading`), not by value (`--font-size-16`). Include font stacks, size scale, weights, line-heights, and letter-spacing in your token system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Accessibility Considerations\\r\\n\\r\\nBeyond contrast ratios (which are well-documented), consider:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Never disable zoom**: `user-scalable=no` breaks accessibility. If your layout breaks at 200% zoom, fix the layout.\\r\\n- **Use rem/em for font sizes**: This respects user browser settings. Never `px` for body text.\\r\\n- **Minimum 16px body text**: Smaller than this strains eyes and fails WCAG on mobile.\\r\\n- **Adequate touch targets**: Text links need padding or line-height that creates 44px+ tap targets.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n**Avoid**: More than 2-3 font families per project. Skipping fallback font definitions. Ignoring font loading performance (FOUT/FOIT). Using decorative fonts for body text.\\r\\n"}}}'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"i":3,"result":{"status":"fulfilled","value":{"chunk_id":"569b90","wall_time_seconds":1.517912,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":1820,"output":"# Interaction Design\\r\\n\\r\\n## The Eight Interactive States\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery interactive element needs these states designed:\\r\\n\\r\\n| State | When | Visual Treatment |\\r\\n|-------|------|------------------|\\r\\n| **Default** | At rest | Base styling |\\r\\n| **Hover** | Pointer over (not touch) | Subtle lift, color shift |\\r\\n| **Focus** | Keyboard/programmatic focus | Visible ring (see below) |\\r\\n| **Active** | Being pressed | Pressed in, darker |\\r\\n| **Disabled** | Not interactive | Reduced opacity, no pointer |\\r\\n| **Loading** | Processing | Spinner, skeleton |\\r\\n| **Error** | Invalid state | Red border, icon, message |\\r\\n| **Success** | Completed | Green check, confirmation |\\r\\n\\r\\n**The common miss**: Designing hover without focus, or vice versa. They\'re different. Keyboard users never see hover states.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Focus Rings: Do Them Right\\r\\n\\r\\n**Never `outline: none` without replacement.** It\'s an accessibility violation. Instead, use `:focus-visible` to show focus only for keyboard users:\\r\\n\\r\\n```css\\r\\n/* Hide focus ring for mouse/touch */\\r\\nbutton:focus {\\r\\n  outline: none;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Show focus ring for keyboard */\\r\\nbutton:focus-visible {\\r\\n  outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent);\\r\\n  outline-offset: 2px;\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Focus ring design**:\\r\\n- High contrast (3:1 minimum against adjacent colors)\\r\\n- 2-3px thick\\r\\n- Offset from element (not inside it)\\r\\n- Consistent across all interactive elements\\r\\n\\r\\n## Form Design: The Non-Obvious\\r\\n\\r\\n**Placeholders aren\'t labels**—they disappear on input. Always use visible `<label>` elements. **Validate on blur**, not on every keystroke (exception: password strength). Place errors **below** fields with `aria-describedby` connecting them.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Loading States\\r\\n\\r\\n**Optimistic updates**: Show success immediately, rollback on failure. Use for low-stakes actions (likes, follows), not payments or destructive actions. **Skeleton screens > spinners**—they preview content shape and feel faster than generic spinners.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Modals: The Inert Approach\\r\\n\\r\\nFocus trapping in modals used to require complex JavaScript. Now use the `inert` attribute:\\r\\n\\r\\n```html\\r\\n<!-- When modal is open -->\\r\\n<main inert>\\r\\n  <!-- Content behind modal can\'t be focused or clicked -->\\r\\n</main>\\r\\n<dialog open>\\r\\n  <h2>Modal Title</h2>\\r\\n  <!-- Focus stays inside modal -->\\r\\n</dialog>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nOr use the native `<dialog>` element:\\r\\n\\r\\n```javascript\\r\\nconst dialog = document.querySelector(\'dialog\');\\r\\ndialog.showModal();  // Opens with focus trap, closes on Escape\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## The Popover API\\r\\n\\r\\nFor tooltips, dropdowns, and non-modal overlays, use native popovers:\\r\\n\\r\\n```html\\r\\n<button popovertarget=\\"menu\\">Open menu</button>\\r\\n<div id=\\"menu\\" popover>\\r\\n  <button>Option 1</button>\\r\\n  <button>Option 2</button>\\r\\n</div>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Benefits**: Light-dismiss (click outside closes), proper stacking, no z-index wars, accessible by default.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Dropdown & Overlay Positioning\\r\\n\\r\\nDropdowns rendered with `position: absolute` inside a container that has `overflow: hidden` or `overflow: auto` will be clipped. This is the single most common dropdown bug in generated code.\\r\\n\\r\\n### CSS Anchor Positioning\\r\\n\\r\\nThe modern solution uses the CSS Anchor Positioning API to tether an overlay to its trigger without JavaScript:\\r\\n\\r\\n```css\\r\\n.trigger {\\r\\n  anchor-name: --menu-trigger;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n.dropdown {\\r\\n  position: fixed;\\r\\n  position-anchor: --menu-trigger;\\r\\n  position-area: block-end span-inline-end;\\r\\n  margin-top: 4px;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Flip above if no room below */\\r\\n@position-try --flip-above {\\r\\n  position-area: block-start span-inline-end;\\r\\n  margin-bottom: 4px;\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nBecause the dropdown uses `position: fixed`, it escapes any `overflow` clipping on ancestor elements. The `@position-try` block handles viewport edges automatically. **Browser support**: Chrome 125+, Edge 125+. Not yet in Firefox or Safari - use a fallback for those browsers.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Popover + Anchor Combo\\r\\n\\r\\nCombining the Popover API with anchor positioning gives you stacking, light-dismiss, accessibility, and correct positioning in one pattern:\\r\\n\\r\\n```html\\r\\n<button popovertarget=\\"menu\\" class=\\"trigger\\">Open</button>\\r\\n<div id=\\"menu\\" popover class=\\"dropdown\\">\\r\\n  <button>Option 1</button>\\r\\n  <button>Option 2</button>\\r\\n</div>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThe `popover` attribute places the element in the **top layer**, which sits above all other content regardless of z-index or overflow. No portal needed.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Portal / Teleport Pattern\\r\\n\\r\\nIn component frameworks, render the dropdown at the document root and position it with JavaScript:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **React**: `createPortal(dropdown, document.body)`\\r\\n- **Vue**: `<Teleport to=\\"body\\">`\\r\\n- **Svelte**: Use a portal library or mount to `document.body`\\r\\n\\r\\nCalculate position from the trigger\'s `getBoundingClientRect()`, then apply `position: fixed` with `top` and `left` values. Recalculate on scroll and resize.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Fixed Positioning Fallback\\r\\n\\r\\nFor browsers without anchor positioning support, `position: fixed` with manual coordinates avoids overflow clipping:\\r\\n\\r\\n```css\\r\\n.dropdown {\\r\\n  position: fixed;\\r\\n  /* top/left set via JS from trigger\'s getBoundingClientRect() */\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nCheck viewport boundaries before rendering. If the dropdown would overflow the bottom edge, flip it above the trigger. If it would overflow the right edge, align it to the trigger\'s right side instead.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Anti-Patterns\\r\\n\\r\\n- **`position: absolute` inside `overflow: hidden`** - The dropdown will be clipped. Use `position: fixed` or the top layer instead.\\r\\n- **Arbitrary z-index values** like `z-index: 9999` - Use a semantic z-index scale: `dropdown (100) -> sticky (200) -> modal-backdrop (300) -> modal (400) -> toast (500) -> tooltip (600)`.\\r\\n- **Rendering dropdown markup inline** without an escape hatch from the parent\'s stacking context. Either use `popover` (top layer), a portal, or `position: fixed`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Destructive Actions: Undo > Confirm\\r\\n\\r\\n**Undo is better than confirmation dialogs**—users click through confirmations mindlessly. Remove from UI immediately, show undo toast, actually delete after toast expires. Use confirmation only for truly irreversible actions (account deletion), high-cost actions, or batch operations.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Keyboard Navigation Patterns\\r\\n\\r\\n### Roving Tabindex\\r\\n\\r\\nFor component groups (tabs, menu items, radio groups), one item is tabbable; arrow keys move within:\\r\\n\\r\\n```html\\r\\n<div role=\\"tablist\\">\\r\\n  <button role=\\"tab\\" tabindex=\\"0\\">Tab 1</button>\\r\\n  <button role=\\"tab\\" tabindex=\\"-1\\">Tab 2</button>\\r\\n  <button role=\\"tab\\" tabindex=\\"-1\\">Tab 3</button>\\r\\n</div>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nArrow keys move `tabindex=\\"0\\"` between items. Tab moves to the next component entirely.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Skip Links\\r\\n\\r\\nProvide skip links (`<a href=\\"#main-content\\">Skip to main content</a>`) for keyboard users to jump past navigation. Hide off-screen, show on focus.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Gesture Discoverability\\r\\n\\r\\nSwipe-to-delete and similar gestures are invisible. Hint at their existence:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Partially reveal**: Show delete button peeking from edge\\r\\n- **Onboarding**: Coach marks on first use\\r\\n- **Alternative**: Always provide a visible fallback (menu with \\"Delete\\")\\r\\n\\r\\nDon\'t rely on gestures as the only way to perform actions.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n**Avoid**: Removing focus indicators without alternatives. Using placeholder text as labels. Touch targets <44x44px. Generic error messages. Custom controls without ARIA/keyboard support.\\r\\n"}}}'}]

These durations feel right for most UI:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Duration | Use Case | Examples |\\r\\n|----------|----------|----------|\\r\\n| **100-150ms** | Instant feedback | Button press, toggle, color change |\\r\\n| **200-300ms** | State changes | Menu open, tooltip, hover states |\\r\\n| **300-500ms** | Layout changes | Accordion, modal, drawer |\\r\\n| **500-800ms** | Entrance animations | Page load, hero reveals |\\r\\n\\r\\n**Exit animations are faster than entrances**—use ~75% of enter duration.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Easing: Pick the Right Curve\\r\\n\\r\\n**Don\'t use `ease`.** It\'s a compromise that\'s rarely optimal. Instead:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Curve | Use For | CSS |\\r\\n|-------|---------|-----|\\r\\n| **ease-out** | Elements entering | `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` |\\r\\n| **ease-in** | Elements leaving | `cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.84, 0)` |\\r\\n| **ease-in-out** | State toggles (there → back) | `cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)` |\\r\\n\\r\\n**For micro-interactions, use exponential curves**—they feel natural because they mimic real physics (friction, deceleration):\\r\\n\\r\\n```css\\r\\n/* Quart out - smooth, refined (recommended default) */\\r\\n--ease-out-quart: cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1);\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Quint out - slightly more dramatic */\\r\\n--ease-out-quint: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1);\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Expo out - snappy, confident */\\r\\n--ease-out-expo: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Avoid bounce and elastic curves.** They were trendy in 2015 but now feel tacky and amateurish. Real objects don\'t bounce when they stop—they decelerate smoothly. Overshoot effects draw attention to the animation itself rather than the content.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Premium Motion Materials\\r\\n\\r\\nTransform and opacity are reliable defaults, not the whole palette. Premium interfaces often need atmospheric properties: blur reveals, backdrop-filter panels, saturation or brightness shifts, shadow bloom, SVG filters, masks, clip paths, gradient-position movement, and variable font or shader-driven effects.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse the right material for the effect:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Transform / opacity**: movement, press feedback, simple reveals, list choreography.\\r\\n- **Blur / filter / backdrop-filter**: focus pulls, depth, glass or lens effects, softened entrances, atmospheric transitions.\\r\\n- **Clip path / masks**: wipes, reveals, editorial cropping, product-like transitions.\\r\\n- **Shadow / glow / color filters**: energy, affordance, focus, warmth, active state.\\r\\n- **Grid-template rows or FLIP-style transforms**: expanding and reflowing layout without animating `height` directly.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe hard rule is not \\"transform and opacity only.\\" The hard rule is: avoid animating layout-driving properties casually (`width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, margins), keep expensive effects bounded to small or isolated areas, and verify in-browser that the result is smooth on the target viewports. If blur/filter makes the interaction feel significantly more premium and remains smooth, use it.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Staggered Animations\\r\\n\\r\\nUse CSS custom properties for cleaner stagger: `animation-delay: calc(var(--i, 0) * 50ms)` with `style=\\"--i: 0\\"` on each item. **Cap total stagger time**—10 items at 50ms = 500ms total. For many items, reduce per-item delay or cap staggered count.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Reduced Motion\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is not optional. Vestibular disorders affect ~35% of adults over 40.\\r\\n\\r\\n```css\\r\\n/* Define animations normally */\\r\\n.card {\\r\\n  animation: slide-up 500ms ease-out;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Provide alternative for reduced motion */\\r\\n@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {\\r\\n  .card {\\r\\n    animation: fade-in 200ms ease-out;  /* Crossfade instead of motion */\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Or disable entirely */\\r\\n@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {\\r\\n  *, *::before, *::after {\\r\\n    animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;\\r\\n    transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**What to preserve**: Functional animations like progress bars, loading spinners (slowed down), and focus indicators should still work—just without spatial movement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Perceived Performance\\r\\n\\r\\n**Nobody cares how fast your site is—just how fast it feels.** Perception can be as effective as actual performance.\\r\\n\\r\\n**The 80ms threshold**: Our brains buffer sensory input for ~80ms to synchronize perception. Anything under 80ms feels instant and simultaneous. This is your target for micro-interactions.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Active vs passive time**: Passive waiting (staring at a spinner) feels longer than active engagement. Strategies to shift the balance:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Preemptive start**: Begin transitions immediately while loading (iOS app zoom, skeleton UI). Users perceive work happening.\\r\\n- **Early completion**: Show content progressively—don\'t wait for everything. Video buffering, progressive images, streaming HTML.\\r\\n- **Optimistic UI**: Update the interface immediately, handle failures gracefully. Instagram likes work offline—the UI updates instantly, syncs later. Use for low-stakes actions; avoid for payments or destructive operations.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Easing affects perceived duration**: Ease-in (accelerating toward completion) makes tasks feel shorter because the peak-end effect weights final moments heavily. Ease-out feels satisfying for entrances, but ease-in toward a task\'s end compresses perceived time.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Caution**: Too-fast responses can decrease perceived value. Users may distrust instant results for complex operations (search, analysis). Sometimes a brief delay signals \\"real work\\" is happening.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Performance\\r\\n\\r\\nDon\'t use `will-change` preemptively—only when animation is imminent (`:hover`, `.animating`). For scroll-triggered animations, use Intersection Observer instead of scroll events; unobserve after animating once. Create motion tokens for consistency (durations, easings, common transitions).\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n**Avoid**: Animating everything (animation fatigue is real). Using >500ms for UI feedback. Ignoring `prefers-reduced-motion`. Using animation to hide slow loading.\\r\\n"}}}'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"i":1,"result":{"status":"fulfilled","value":{"chunk_id":"0b0214","wall_time_seconds":0.3797631,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":895,"output":"# Responsive Design\\r\\n\\r\\n## Mobile-First: Write It Right\\r\\n\\r\\nStart with base styles for mobile, use `min-width` queries to layer complexity. Desktop-first (`max-width`) means mobile loads unnecessary styles first.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Breakpoints: Content-Driven\\r\\n\\r\\nDon\'t chase device sizes—let content tell you where to break. Start narrow, stretch until design breaks, add breakpoint there. Three breakpoints usually suffice (640, 768, 1024px). Use `clamp()` for fluid values without breakpoints.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Detect Input Method, Not Just Screen Size\\r\\n\\r\\n**Screen size doesn\'t tell you input method.** A laptop with touchscreen, a tablet with keyboard—use pointer and hover queries:\\r\\n\\r\\n```css\\r\\n/* Fine pointer (mouse, trackpad) */\\r\\n@media (pointer: fine) {\\r\\n  .button { padding: 8px 16px; }\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Coarse pointer (touch, stylus) */\\r\\n@media (pointer: coarse) {\\r\\n  .button { padding: 12px 20px; }  /* Larger touch target */\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Device supports hover */\\r\\n@media (hover: hover) {\\r\\n  .card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); }\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* Device doesn\'t support hover (touch) */\\r\\n@media (hover: none) {\\r\\n  .card { /* No hover state - use active instead */ }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Critical**: Don\'t rely on hover for functionality. Touch users can\'t hover.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Safe Areas: Handle the Notch\\r\\n\\r\\nModern phones have notches, rounded corners, and home indicators. Use `env()`:\\r\\n\\r\\n```css\\r\\nbody {\\r\\n  padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top);\\r\\n  padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom);\\r\\n  padding-left: env(safe-area-inset-left);\\r\\n  padding-right: env(safe-area-inset-right);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* With fallback */\\r\\n.footer {\\r\\n  padding-bottom: max(1rem, env(safe-area-inset-bottom));\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Enable viewport-fit** in your meta tag:\\r\\n```html\\r\\n<meta name=\\"viewport\\" content=\\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover\\">\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Responsive Images: Get It Right\\r\\n\\r\\n### srcset with Width Descriptors\\r\\n\\r\\n```html\\r\\n<img\\r\\n  src=\\"hero-800.jpg\\"\\r\\n  srcset=\\"\\r\\n    hero-400.jpg 400w,\\r\\n    hero-800.jpg 800w,\\r\\n    hero-1200.jpg 1200w\\r\\n  \\"\\r\\n  sizes=\\"(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 50vw\\"\\r\\n  alt=\\"Hero image\\"\\r\\n>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**How it works**:\\r\\n- `srcset` lists available images with their actual widths (`w` descriptors)\\r\\n- `sizes` tells the browser how wide the image will display\\r\\n- Browser picks the best file based on viewport width AND device pixel ratio\\r\\n\\r\\n### Picture Element for Art Direction\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen you need different crops/compositions (not just resolutions):\\r\\n\\r\\n```html\\r\\n<picture>\\r\\n  <source media=\\"(min-width: 768px)\\" srcset=\\"wide.jpg\\">\\r\\n  <source media=\\"(max-width: 767px)\\" srcset=\\"tall.jpg\\">\\r\\n  <img src=\\"fallback.jpg\\" alt=\\"...\\">\\r\\n</picture>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Layout Adaptation Patterns\\r\\n\\r\\n**Navigation**: Three stages—hamburger + drawer on mobile, horizontal compact on tablet, full with labels on desktop. **Tables**: Transform to cards on mobile using `display: block` and `data-label` attributes. **Progressive disclosure**: Use `<details>/<summary>` for content that can collapse on mobile.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Testing: Don\'t Trust DevTools Alone\\r\\n\\r\\nDevTools device emulation is useful for layout but misses:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Actual touch interactions\\r\\n- Real CPU/memory constraints\\r\\n- Network latency patterns\\r\\n- Font rendering differences\\r\\n- Browser chrome/keyboard appearances\\r\\n\\r\\n**Test on at least**: One real iPhone, one real Android, a tablet if relevant. Cheap Android phones reveal performance issues you\'ll never see on simulators.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n**Avoid**: Desktop-first design. Device detection instead of feature detection. Separate mobile/desktop codebases. Ignoring tablet and landscape. Assuming all mobile devices are powerful.\\r\\n"}}}'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"i":2,"result":{"status":"fulfilled","value":{"chunk_id":"458fe2","wall_time_seconds":0.4214882,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":1473,"output":"# Color & Contrast\\r\\n\\r\\n## Color Spaces: Use OKLCH\\r\\n\\r\\n**Stop using HSL.** Use OKLCH (or LCH) instead. It\'s perceptually uniform, meaning equal steps in lightness *look* equal—unlike HSL where 50% lightness in yellow looks bright while 50% in blue looks dark.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe OKLCH function takes three components: `oklch(lightness chroma hue)` where lightness is 0-100%, chroma is roughly 0-0.4, and hue is 0-360. To build a primary color and its lighter / darker variants, hold the chroma+hue roughly constant and vary the lightness — but **reduce chroma as you approach white or black**, because high chroma at extreme lightness looks garish.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe hue you pick is a brand decision and should not come from a default. Do not reach for blue (hue 250) or warm orange (hue 60) by reflex — those are the dominant AI-design defaults, not the right answer for any specific brand.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Building Functional Palettes\\r\\n\\r\\n### Tinted Neutrals\\r\\n\\r\\n**Pure gray is dead.** A neutral with zero chroma feels lifeless next to a colored brand. Add a tiny chroma value (0.005-0.015) to all your neutrals, hued toward whatever your brand color is. The chroma is small enough not to read as \\"tinted\\" consciously, but it creates subconscious cohesion between brand color and UI surfaces.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe hue you tint toward should come from THIS project\'s brand, not from a \\"warm = friendly, cool = tech\\" formula. If your brand color is teal, your neutrals lean toward teal. If your brand color is amber, they lean toward amber. The point is cohesion with the SPECIFIC brand, not a stock palette.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Avoid** the trap of always tinting toward warm orange or always tinting toward cool blue. Those are the two laziest defaults and they create their own monoculture across projects.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Palette Structure\\r\\n\\r\\nA complete system needs:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Role | Purpose | Example |\\r\\n|------|---------|---------|\\r\\n| **Primary** | Brand, CTAs, key actions | 1 color, 3-5 shades |\\r\\n| **Neutral** | Text, backgrounds, borders | 9-11 shade scale |\\r\\n| **Semantic** | Success, error, warning, info | 4 colors, 2-3 shades each |\\r\\n| **Surface** | Cards, modals, overlays | 2-3 elevation levels |\\r\\n\\r\\n**Skip secondary/tertiary unless you need them.** Most apps work fine with one accent color. Adding more creates decision fatigue and visual noise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### The 60-30-10 Rule (Applied Correctly)\\r\\n\\r\\nThis rule is about **visual weight**, not pixel count:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **60%**: Neutral backgrounds, white space, base surfaces\\r\\n- **30%**: Secondary colors—text, borders, inactive states\\r\\n- **10%**: Accent—CTAs, highlights, focus states\\r\\n\\r\\nThe common mistake: using the accent color everywhere because it\'s \\"the brand color.\\" Accent colors work *because* they\'re rare. Overuse kills their power.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Contrast & Accessibility\\r\\n\\r\\n### WCAG Requirements\\r\\n\\r\\n| Content Type | AA Minimum | AAA Target |\\r\\n|--------------|------------|------------|\\r\\n| Body text | 4.5:1 | 7:1 |\\r\\n| Large text (18px+ or 14px bold) | 3:1 | 4.5:1 |\\r\\n| UI components, icons | 3:1 | 4.5:1 |\\r\\n| Non-essential decorations | None | None |\\r\\n\\r\\n**The gotcha**: Placeholder text still needs 4.5:1. That light gray placeholder you see everywhere? Usually fails WCAG.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Dangerous Color Combinations\\r\\n\\r\\nThese commonly fail contrast or cause readability issues:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Light gray text on white (the #1 accessibility fail)\\r\\n- **Gray text on any colored background**—gray looks washed out and dead on color. Use a darker shade of the background color, or transparency\\r\\n- Red text on green background (or vice versa)—8% of men can\'t distinguish these\\r\\n- Blue text on red background (vibrates visually)\\r\\n- Yellow text on white (almost always fails)\\r\\n- Thin light text on images (unpredictable contrast)\\r\\n\\r\\n### Never Use Pure Gray or Pure Black\\r\\n\\r\\nPure gray (`oklch(50% 0 0)`) and pure black (`#000`) don\'t exist in nature—real shadows and surfaces always have a color cast. Even a chroma of 0.005-0.01 is enough to feel natural without being obviously tinted. (See tinted neutrals example above.)\\r\\n\\r\\n### Testing\\r\\n\\r\\nDon\'t trust your eyes. Use tools:\\r\\n\\r\\n- [WebAIM Contrast Checker](https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/)\\r\\n- Browser DevTools → Rendering → Emulate vision deficiencies\\r\\n- [Polypane](https://polypane.app/) for real-time testing\\r\\n\\r\\n## Theming: Light & Dark Mode\\r\\n\\r\\n### Dark Mode Is Not Inverted Light Mode\\r\\n\\r\\nYou can\'t just swap colors. Dark mode requires different design decisions:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Light Mode | Dark Mode |\\r\\n|------------|-----------|\\r\\n| Shadows for depth | Lighter surfaces for depth (no shadows) |\\r\\n| Dark text on light | Light text on dark (reduce font weight) |\\r\\n| Vibrant accents | Desaturate accents slightly |\\r\\n| White backgrounds | Never pure black—use dark gray (oklch 12-18%) |\\r\\n\\r\\nIn dark mode, depth comes from surface lightness, not shadow. Build a 3-step surface scale where higher elevations are lighter (e.g. 15% / 20% / 25% lightness). Use the SAME hue and chroma as your brand color (whatever it is for THIS project — do not reach for blue) and only vary the lightness. Reduce body text weight slightly (e.g. 350 instead of 400) because light text on dark reads as heavier than dark text on light.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Token Hierarchy\\r\\n\\r\\nUse two layers: primitive tokens (`--blue-500`) and semantic tokens (`--color-primary: var(--blue-500)`). For dark mode, only redefine the semantic layer—primitives stay the same.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Alpha Is A Design Smell\\r\\n\\r\\nHeavy use of transparency (rgba, hsla) usually means an incomplete palette. Alpha creates unpredictable contrast, performance overhead, and inconsistency. Define explicit overlay colors for each context instead. Exception: focus rings and interactive states where see-through is needed.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n**Avoid**: Relying on color alone to convey information. Creating palettes without clear roles for each color. Using pure black (#000) for large areas. Skipping color blindness testing (8% of men affected).\\r\\n"}}}'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"i":3,"result":{"status":"fulfilled","value":{"chunk_id":"9e45c8","wall_time_seconds":0.4853284,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":1110,"output":"# UX Writing\\r\\n\\r\\n## The Button Label Problem\\r\\n\\r\\n**Never use \\"OK\\", \\"Submit\\", or \\"Yes/No\\".** These are lazy and ambiguous. Use specific verb + object patterns:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Bad | Good | Why |\\r\\n|-----|------|-----|\\r\\n| OK | Save changes | Says what will happen |\\r\\n| Submit | Create account | Outcome-focused |\\r\\n| Yes | Delete message | Confirms the action |\\r\\n| Cancel | Keep editing | Clarifies what \\"cancel\\" means |\\r\\n| Click here | Download PDF | Describes the destination |\\r\\n\\r\\n**For destructive actions**, name the destruction:\\r\\n- \\"Delete\\" not \\"Remove\\" (delete is permanent, remove implies recoverable)\\r\\n- \\"Delete 5 items\\" not \\"Delete selected\\" (show the count)\\r\\n\\r\\n## Error Messages: The Formula\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery error message should answer: (1) What happened? (2) Why? (3) How to fix it? Example: \\"Email address isn\'t valid. Please include an @ symbol.\\" not \\"Invalid input\\".\\r\\n\\r\\n### Error Message Templates\\r\\n\\r\\n| Situation | Template |\\r\\n|-----------|----------|\\r\\n| **Format error** | \\"[Field] needs to be [format]. Example: [example]\\" |\\r\\n| **Missing required** | \\"Please enter [what\'s missing]\\" |\\r\\n| **Permission denied** | \\"You don\'t have access to [thing]. [What to do instead]\\" |\\r\\n| **Network error** | \\"We couldn\'t reach [thing]. Check your connection and [action].\\" |\\r\\n| **Server error** | \\"Something went wrong on our end. We\'re looking into it. [Alternative action]\\" |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Don\'t Blame the User\\r\\n\\r\\nReframe errors: \\"Please enter a date in MM/DD/YYYY format\\" not \\"You entered an invalid date\\".\\r\\n\\r\\n## Empty States Are Opportunities\\r\\n\\r\\nEmpty states are onboarding moments: (1) Acknowledge briefly, (2) Explain the value of filling it, (3) Provide a clear action. \\"No projects yet. Create your first one to get started.\\" not just \\"No items\\".\\r\\n\\r\\n## Voice vs Tone\\r\\n\\r\\n**Voice** is your brand\'s personality—consistent everywhere.\\r\\n**Tone** adapts to the moment.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Moment | Tone Shift |\\r\\n|--------|------------|\\r\\n| Success | Celebratory, brief: \\"Done! Your changes are live.\\" |\\r\\n| Error | Empathetic, helpful: \\"That didn\'t work. Here\'s what to try...\\" |\\r\\n| Loading | Reassuring: \\"Saving your work...\\" |\\r\\n| Destructive confirm | Serious, clear: \\"Delete this project? This can\'t be undone.\\" |\\r\\n\\r\\n**Never use humor for errors.** Users are already frustrated. Be helpful, not cute.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Writing for Accessibility\\r\\n\\r\\n**Link text** must have standalone meaning—\\"View pricing plans\\" not \\"Click here\\". **Alt text** describes information, not the image—\\"Revenue increased 40% in Q4\\" not \\"Chart\\". Use `alt=\\"\\"` for decorative images. **Icon buttons** need `aria-label` for screen reader context.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Writing for Translation\\r\\n\\r\\n### Plan for Expansion\\r\\n\\r\\nGerman text is ~30% longer than English. Allocate space:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Language | Expansion |\\r\\n|----------|-----------|\\r\\n| German | +30% |\\r\\n| French | +20% |\\r\\n| Finnish | +30-40% |\\r\\n| Chinese | -30% (fewer chars, but same width) |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Translation-Friendly Patterns\\r\\n\\r\\nKeep numbers separate (\\"New messages: 3\\" not \\"You have 3 new messages\\"). Use full sentences as single strings (word order varies by language). Avoid abbreviations (\\"5 minutes ago\\" not \\"5 mins ago\\"). Give translators context about where strings appear.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Consistency: The Terminology Problem\\r\\n\\r\\nPick one term and stick with it:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Inconsistent | Consistent |\\r\\n|--------------|------------|\\r\\n| Delete / Remove / Trash | Delete |\\r\\n| Settings / Preferences / Options | Settings |\\r\\n| Sign in / Log in / Enter | Sign in |\\r\\n| Create / Add / New | Create |\\r\\n\\r\\nBuild a terminology glossary and enforce it. Variety creates confusion.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Avoid Redundant Copy\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the heading explains it, the intro is redundant. If the button is clear, don\'t explain it again. Say it once, say it well.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Loading States\\r\\n\\r\\nBe specific: \\"Saving your draft...\\" not \\"Loading...\\". For long waits, set expectations (\\"This usually takes 30 seconds\\") or show progress.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Confirmation Dialogs: Use Sparingly\\r\\n\\r\\nMost confirmation dialogs are design failures—consider undo instead. When you must confirm: name the action, explain consequences, use specific button labels (\\"Delete project\\" / \\"Keep project\\", not \\"Yes\\" / \\"No\\").\\r\\n\\r\\n## Form Instructions\\r\\n\\r\\nShow format with placeholders, not instructions. For non-obvious fields, explain why you\'re asking.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n**Avoid**: Jargon without explanation. Blaming users (\\"You made an error\\" → \\"This field is required\\"). Vague errors (\\"Something went wrong\\"). Varying terminology for variety. Humor for errors.\\r\\n"}}}'}]

This replaced a single\r\n   * `questionNumber: number | null`, which could not express "Q1, 6, 8, 23" —\r\n   * the thing you most often want when rebuilding a specific set.\r\n   */\r\n  questionNumbers: number[];\r\n  questionTypes: string[];\r\n  reasoningTypes: string[];\r\n  questionFeatures: string[];\r\n  difficulties: number[];\r\n  searchQuery: string;\r\n}\r\n\r\nexport interface LRDrillFacetValues {\r\n  prepTests: number;\r\n  sections: number;\r\n  questionTypes: string;\r\n  reasoningTypes: string;\r\n  questionFeatures: string;\r\n  difficulties: number;\r\n}\r\n\r\nexport type LRDrillFilterFacet = keyof LRDrillFacetValues;\r\n\r\nexport const LR_DRILL_FILTER_FACETS: readonly LRDrillFilterFacet[] = [\r\n  \'prepTests\',\r\n  \'sections\',\r\n  \'questionTypes\',\r\n  \'reasoningTypes\',\r\n  \'questionFeatures\',\r\n  \'difficulties\',\r\n];\r\n\r\nexport function createEmptyLRDrillFilters(): LRDrillFilters {\r\n  return {\r\n    prepTests: [],\r\n    sections: [],\r\n    questionNumbers: [],\r\n    questionTypes: [],\r\n    reasoningTypes: [],\r\n    questionFeatures: [],\r\n    difficulties: [],\r\n    searchQuery: \'\',\r\n  };\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction intersects<T>(selected: readonly T[], actual: readonly T[] | undefined): boolean {\r\n  if (selected.length === 0) return true;\r\n  if (!actual?.length) return false;\r\n\r\n  const selectedValues = new Set(selected);\r\n  return actual.some((value) => selectedValues.has(value));\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction normalizeSearchText(value: string): string {\r\n  return value.toLocaleLowerCase().replace(/\\s+/g, \' \').trim();\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction getQuestionSearchText(question: LRQuestion): string {\r\n  return normalizeSearchText(\r\n    [\r\n      question.qid,\r\n      question.stimulus ?? \'\',\r\n      question.questionStem,\r\n      ...Object.values(question.answerChoices ?? {}),\r\n    ].join(\' \'),\r\n  );\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction getQuestionFacetValues<F extends LRDrillFilterFacet>(\r\n  question: LRQuestion,\r\n  facet: F,\r\n): LRDrillFacetValues[F][] {\r\n  switch (facet) {\r\n    case \'prepTests\':\r\n      return [question.pt] as LRDrillFacetValues[F][];\r\n    case \'sections\':\r\n      return [question.section] as LRDrillFacetValues[F][];\r\n    case \'questionTypes\':\r\n      return [question.qtype] as LRDrillFacetValues[F][];\r\n    case \'reasoningTypes\':\r\n      return (question.reasoningType ?? Applied via\r\n   an explicit class rather than a blanket `.uppercase` selector — the\r\n   observatory hosts launcher stages whose labels are not part of this set. */\r\n.drill-observatory-root .drill-observatory-label {\r\n  color: var(--observatory-ink-50);\r\n  font-family: var(--observatory-label-font);\r\n  font-size: var(--observatory-text-label);\r\n  font-weight: 500;\r\n  letter-spacing: var(--observatory-track-label);\r\n  text-transform: uppercase;\r\n}\r\n\r\n/* The dateline prints twice and CSS picks one, so the first paint is already\r\n   right. Between 900 and 1099 the greeting column is too narrow for the long\r\n   month and the date wrapped to two lines. */\r\n.drill-observatory-root .drill-observatory-date-short {\r\n  display: none;\r\n}\r\n\r\n@media (min-width: 900px) and (max-width: 1099px) {\r\n  .drill-observatory-root .drill-observatory-date-long {\r\n    display: none;\r\n  }\r\n\r\n  /* The short month alone was not enough: at 1024 the greeting column is 201px\r\n     and the short dateline measured 197px of glyphs plus 47px of tracking, so\r\n     "2026" still fell to a second line. The tracking is decoration at this\r\n     size, and tightening it buys back 25px. Declared on the span itself: a\r\n'}]

function togglePopoverOption(triggerName: RegExp, checkboxId: string) {
  fireEvent.click(trigger(triggerName));
  const checkbox = document.getElementById(checkboxId);
  expect(checkbox).not.toBeNull();
  fireEvent.click(checkbox!);
  fireEvent.click(trigger(triggerName));
}

function pasteReferences(text: string) {
  fireEvent.click(screen.getByText('Paste question references'));
  const input = screen.getByLabelText('Paste exact questions or a PrepTest range');
  fireEvent.change(input, { target: { value: text } });
  fireEvent.keyDown(input, { key: 'Enter' });
}

function previewSet() {
  fireEvent.click(screen.getAllByRole('button', { name: 'Create set preview (5)' })[0]);
}

describe('QuestionPicker LR drill setup', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    mockToast.mockClear();
    mockRecordExposures.mockClear();
  });

  it('places search and address controls before the four focus controls', () => {
    setup();
    const controls = [
      screen.getByRole('searchbox', { name: 'Find a question by text or PrepTest reference' }),
      trigger(/^PrepTest selector/),
      trigger(/^Section selector/),
      screen.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Question number' }),
      trigger(/^Question Type/),
      trigger(/^Reasoning Types/),
      trigger(/^Question Features/),
      trigger(/^Levels/),
    ];
    for (let index = 0; index < controls.length - 1; index += 1) {
      expect(controls[index].compareDocumentPosition(controls[index + 1]) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING).toBeTruthy();
    }
    expect(screen.getByText('Choose questions')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText('Narrow the rest')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('combines PrepTest, section, reasoning, feature, and level filters', () => {
    setup();
    togglePopoverOption(/^PrepTest selector/, 'pt-101');
    togglePopoverOption(/^Section selector/, 'section-1');
    togglePopoverOption(/^Reasoning Types/, 'rt-Causation');
    togglePopoverOption(/^Question Features/, 'feat-Alternative Cause');
    togglePopoverOption(/^Levels/, 'diff-1');
    expect(screen.getByText('1 matching question')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('retains a selected option when its contextual count becomes zero', () => {
    setup();
    togglePopoverOption(/^Reasoning Types/, 'rt-Comparative Reasoning');
    pasteReferences('Q1');
    expect(screen.getByText('0 matching questions')).toBeInTheDocument();
    fireEvent.click(trigger(/^Reasoning Types/));
    expect(document.getElementById('rt-Comparative Reasoning')).toBeChecked();
    expect(document.querySelector('label[for="rt-Comparative Reasoning"]')).toHaveTextContent('Comparison (0)');
  });

  it('clears one facet or all filters without removing exact picks', () => {
    setup();
    pasteReferences('PT101.S1.Q1');
    togglePopoverOption(/^PrepTest selector/, 'pt-101');
    fireEvent.click(trigger(/^Reasoning Types/));
    fireEvent.click(document.getElementById('rt-Causation')!);
    const header = screen.getByText('Select Reasoning Types').parentElement!;
    fireEvent.click(within(header).getByRole('button', { name: 'Clear' }));
    expect(trigger(/^PrepTest selector/)).toHaveAccessibleName(/101/);
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Clear all' }));
    expect(screen.getByText('1 added')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText('7 matching questions')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('finds a question by its dotted address', () => {
    setup();
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByRole('searchbox', { name: 'Find a question by text or PrepTest reference' }), {
      target: { value: 'PT102.S2.Q6' },
    });
    expect(screen.getByText('1 matching question')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('previews and launches the exact set shown', () => {
    const { onStartDrill } = setup();
    previewSet();
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Start this drill (5)' }));
    expect(onStartDrill).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({
      count: 5,
      selectedQids: [
        'PT101-S1-Q1',
        'PT101-S1-Q2',
        'PT101-S2-Q3',
        'PT101-S2-Q4',
        'PT101-S1-Q5',
      ],
    }));
  });

  it('guarantees exact picks and fills the remaining places from filters', () => {
    const { onStartDrill } = setup();
    pasteReferences('PT102.S2.Q6');
    togglePopoverOption(/^PrepTest selector/, 'pt-101');
    previewSet();
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Start this drill (5)' }));
    expect(onStartDrill.mock.calls[0][0].selectedQids).toEqual([
      'PT102-S2-Q6',
      'PT101-S1-Q1',
      'PT101-S1-Q2',
      'PT101-S2-Q3',
      'PT101-S2-Q4',
    ]);
  });

  it('applies a pasted range and rejects invalid references atomically', () => {
    setup();
    pasteReferences('PT101 S1 Q1,2');
    expect(screen.getByText('2 matching questions')).toBeInTheDocument();
    pasteReferences('PT101.S1.Q1, PT101.S9.Q99');
    expect(screen.getByRole('alert')).toHaveTextContent('Nothing was added');
    expect(screen.getByText('0 added')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
`;
